title: Predecessor credential during a rotation overlap
description: A value that an issuer's rotation procedure has replaced but that the provider documents as still working for a stated overlap or grace period.
semantics: During a documented overlap both the old and the new credential authenticate. Offline text cannot show whether a given occurrence of the old value is inside or past its overlap, so the text alone does not establish that it is dead. Policy (maintainer-only, ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 6): a predecessor value is expected to be flagged.

applicability.rationale: Stripe (up to 7 days) and Slack token rotation (grace period on the previous refresh token; existing access token not immediately invalidated) document an overlap. Other providers are not claimed.

evidenceBasis.rationale: Project policy, maintainer-only (ADR 0020, ADR 0019 item 6 (#112)): a predecessor value from a rotation overlap is expected to be flagged. The overlap itself is provider-documented (sources); what to expect of a predecessor value is a project choice, since offline text cannot show whether an occurrence is inside or past its overlap. Finalized by the sole maintainer alone: not reviewed, not independent validation, queued for retro-review (#154). The question, options, strongest dissent and reversing evidence are in the review history.

sources.supports: When a key is rotated in the Dashboard both the old and new keys work for up to 7 days.
sources.locator: section 'Rotate safely to avoid downtime', item 'Use the grace period'

sources.supports: Calling oauth.v2.access does not immediately invalidate the existing access token; the used refresh token is revoked after a short grace period.

notes: Project-authored by the Redact Secret project, which maintains this repository; not independent evidence. Maintainer-only (ADR 0020): decided by the sole maintainer, not reviewed, not independent validation; queued for retro-review (#154).
